summary.text: A girl, the only child of healthy non-consanguineous parents, was born at 40 weeks after a normal pregnancy and uncomplicated delivery, with normal hearing on screening and BERA. Social withdrawal and behavioural manifestations began around 18 months. At 36 months she was non-verbal, uncooperative, avoided eye contact, did not respond to her name, showed repetitive movements and stereotypies, and had severe receptive and expressive language deficits.

A multidisciplinary admission team at an institute in Belgrade made a working diagnosis of ASD with overlapping SLI symptoms, noting that certainty was hard to reach because she was 36 months old and had not been treated before. Treatment began after the initial evaluation. Behavioural, cognitive, autism, sensory and speech-language instruments and EEG at rest and during auditory-verbal stimulation were repeated every six months from 36 to 66 months.

Integrative therapy comprised speech-language therapy, sensory integration, psychomotor re-education and counseling sessions for the mother. The child showed no progress in the first six months, behavioural retests changed minimally and only EEG findings differed. Receptive and expressive language progress was noticed at 48 months, and at 54 months she was verbal with functional agrammatical speech.

Speech and language developed during therapy while autistic symptoms reduced. By 66 months the autism index indicated no autism, autistic symptoms were no longer clinically significant, and sensory processing resembled that of typically developing children on most subscales. Frontal theta lateralized to the left hemisphere from 54 months after being right-dominant earlier.
